AbstractExtreme weather and climate events are increasingly intensified by human-induced global warming, exacerbating risks to ecosystems and society. Introduction:Pediatric craniofacial trauma, characterized by forceful blows or injuries to the facial bones or fragile skull of a child, can present symptoms of traumatic brain injury (TBI). TBI is a key player in the increased mortality rate of pediatric populations. Through a bibliometric analysis, this study aims to assess and understand the research landscape of pediatric craniofacial trauma and TBI.

AbstractOccasional boom-bust cycles have long characterized national wine industries, but without them coinciding with the cycles of other countries. Today's wine crisis is different in that prices for all but high-quality wines are depressed in all major wine-producing countries, and the world is awash with a large surplus of (especially red) non-premium wine. This article first outlines the nature and extent of the crisis.

abstract: The Bendung watershed plays an important role as the main drainage system that flows into the Musi River in Palembang City. Changes in land cover, which is dominated by built-up areas and densely populated areas, have disrupted the hydrological cycle and increased the potential for flooding. A total of 21 tributaries around residential areas are not functioning optimally due to siltation and residential density, thereby reducing the soil's ability to absorb water and triggering surface runoff.

The study proposes an IoT-enabled optimized Physics-Guided Transfer Learning (PGTL) ARIMAX–LSTM framework. The framework integrates the linear trend prediction ability of ARIMAX along with the nonlinear learning of residuals through LSTM networks.

AbstractHealthy freshwater ecosystems are crucial for sustainable development, yet they face growing threats from unsustainable water use. However, current water scarcity metrics focus almost exclusively on human demand, overlooking whether sufficient water remains to sustain ecosystems. We address this gap by presenting the first evaluation of ecological water scarcity (EWS) across 1,182 river basins, introducing a novel indicator that recognizes ecosystems as legitimate water users to those of humans.

AbstractAccurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions.

Global environmental change can rapidly reshape phenotypic trait distributions through adaptive and neutral processes. Yet, disentangling their relative contributions remains a major challenge, particularly for traits underpinning ecosystem functioning. Using a two‐year mesocosm study, we experimentally evolved Asellus aquaticus under contrasting temperature and predation regimes to test how the joint influence of these global change pressures shape the evolution of traits and ecosystem functioning.

Background In Sudano-Sahelian regions of sub-Saharan Africa, malaria transmission is strictly seasonal and governed by climate variability. Climate change is altering these predictable patterns, increasing rainfall unpredictability and shifting vector ecological niches, which threatens ongoing control efforts. This study analyzes the relationship between environmental variables, vector dynamics, and malaria morbidity in Keur Socé, Senegal.

The ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous substitutions (dN/dS) encodes important information about the selection pressures acting on protein-coding genes. In bacterial populations, dN/dS often declines with the sequence divergence between strains, but the mechanisms responsible for this broad empirical trend are still debated. Existing models have primarily focused on de novo mutations, overlooking the older genetic variants that are continually introduced through horizontal gene transfer and recombination.

Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam.) is a high-yielding crop that serves as both a food source and a raw material for industrial processing. Drought stress severely impairs sweet potato yield and quality. A MYB-type transcription factor, IbMYB11, was previously identified as a differentially expressed gene induced by drought stress from our previous comparative transcriptome analysis.

Poverty eradication remains a central challenge for sustainable development, yet its environmental determinants are not sufficiently explored. Theoretically, air pollution may exacerbate poverty. However, empirical research on how air pollution influences global poverty is lacking.

Climate change mitigation increasingly hinges on decarbonising the built environment, yet renewable energy integration in building construction remains underexplored in many emerging economies in Africa, including Ghana. This study examined the enhanced deployment of renewable energy sources (RES) in real estate projects as a contribution to climate change mitigation using the IDT approach. Using quantitative design methodologies, data was collected from 400 professionals working in the real estate industry, receiving a response rate of 94 %.

Abiotic stresses reduce barley growth and yield by elevating the free radicals such as reactive oxygen (ROS), nitrogen (RNS), carbonyl (RCS), and sulfur species (RSS) in plant cells. Among these, hydrogen sulfide (H2S), classified as RSS, serves as a signalling molecule and growth regulator in stress responses. However, the optimal sodium hydrosulphide (NaHS; an H2S donor) concentrations for barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) remain unknown.

The methods used in monitoring the increasing drought are vitally significant. In order to determine and monitor drought, many scientific studies have been carried out in our country, especially using the standardized precipitation index (SPI). However, due to increasing temperatures and evaporation, there is a need for studies showing the spatio-temporal change of drought at the country scale according to the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI), which also takes evaporation into account.

An improved biogeography-based optimization (IBBO) algorithm is proposed for determining the optimal parameter values of a multi-partition nonlinear Muskingum flood routing model. AbstractInoculation theory is a long‐studied communication strategy for building resistance to influence. Weather myth‐busting often already does part of the work of inoculation by raising and refuting myths. This short article considers #MythBusterMonday, a social media initiative from the National Weather Service Weather Forecast Office in State College, Pennsylvania (USA), as an example of this close fit.

ABSTRACTThe gut virome is a critical component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis; however, its role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains poorly understood due to limited sample sizes and geographic bias. We aimed to construct a comprehensive global atlas of the IBS gut virome to elucidate its composition, functional potential, and clinical relevance across diverse populations and IBS subtypes. We integrated multi-cohort data comprising 1,104 samples (790 IBS patients and 314 healthy controls) from 11 cohorts across 10 geographic regions.
